_meta.title: Whitney accent-in-declension rules — formal (stem-class, accent-position) → per-case accent table
_meta.encoded_by: Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) — frontier-judgment encoding session S8, 2026-07-02; every interpretive cell carries a recorded decision + rejected alternative
_meta.source: Whitney, Sanskrit Grammar, 2nd ed. (1889), via the Wikisource ingest src/whitney_sections.json (fetch_whitney.py --all, chapters I–XVIII). Sections read verbatim for this encoding: §§83–84 (by reference), 311, 314–320, 348–352, 355–356, 361, 371–373, 389–391, 421–427, 444–448, 483 (by reference), 410 (by reference).

_meta.consumer: The Zaliznyak-style accent axis (stress scheme S) of RussianTranslation/ZALIZNYAK_INDEX.md; join key = (stem_class T-code, accent_position) from RussianTranslation/src/headword_index.tsv (PWG key2 udātta '/'). Validation: docs/ACCENT_VALIDATION_SPEC.md (VedaWeb 2.0).
_meta.scope_note: Nominal declension only. Vedic-only axis: Classical headwords carry no recorded accent. Verb accent (§§591–598) and adverbial case-form accent (§1110 ff., flagged by §318e) are OUT of scope.
_meta.guardrail: Advisory data. NEVER write rule-predicted or corpus-derived accent/class into reviewed spine or app data (the I/VI accent-collapse lesson). Validation output is a report, not a data edit.

accent_position_values.barytone: lexical udātta NOT on the stem-final syllable (PWG key2: '/' not after the last stem vowel), e.g. áṃśa, svásṛ, rā́jan, mánas
accent_position_values.oxytone: lexical udātta on the stem-final syllable (key2 '/' after the last stem vowel), e.g. agní, devá, senā́, pitṛ́, adánt, ātmán
accent_position_values.monosyllable: stem of one syllable (vāc, dhī, bhū, pad, nāu); accent position is trivially final — Whitney treats these as their own accentual class (§§316–317)
accent_position_values.unmarked: no '/' in key2 (Classical entry) — no prediction possible; axis value '—'

case_slot_values.stem: accent on the lexically accented stem syllable (barytone anchor)
case_slot_values.stem_final: accent on the stem-final syllable, in whatever ablaut grade it surfaces (agní-, pitár-/pitā́r-, adánt-)
case_slot_values.ending: accent on (the first syllable of) the case ending
case_slot_values.first_syllable: accent on the first syllable of the word (vocative rule)
case_slot_values.fused: stem-final vowel and ending vowel have coalesced into one syllable, which carries the accent — acute on plain vowel-blend (dattā́s), svarita on semivowelization (nadyàs, -dhyàm; §§83–4, 316a, 352)
case_slot_values.conditional: value depends on a morphophonemic alternation inside the slot — see the rule's condition field
case_slot_values.variant: Whitney himself licenses/attests both positions — see the rule's interpretation block

conventions.tone_note: Primary comparandum is accent POSITION (which syllable). Tone quality (udātta vs independent svarita) is annotated only where Whitney derives it mechanically: semivowelization yields svarita (§§83–4 via §316a, §352, §356b).

strong.whitney: §311a — 'the five cases whose endings are never accented: 316a'
strong.note: V.du and V.pl are listed with the nominative in Whitney's paradigms (§314f) but obey the vocative rule, not the strong-case rule.

middle.whitney: §311a — weak cases with consonant-initial endings (bhyām, bhis, bhyas, su)

weakest.whitney: §311a — weak cases with vowel-initial endings (ā, e, as, i, os, ām; plus A.pl as/n which patterns with the weak cases)
weakest.note: A.pl is a weak case for accent (§316a lists only N.pl among the five never-accented endings) but is the systematically deviant slot in monosyllables — see R05/D1.

neuter_remap.whitney: §311b — validator MUST remap neuter forms before scoring

vocative.whitney: §314 — its own regime, outside the strong/weak system

case_slots.vowel_stem_note: For monosyllabic stems the middle/weakest distinction is inert: §317 'without distinction of middle and weakest'. For polysyllabic vowel stems mobility is driven by syllabicity of the stem-final, not by the middle/weakest split.

schemes.a: fixed, non-final — accent stays on the lexically accented (non-final) stem syllable through the whole inflection (§315). Zaliznyak-a analog.
schemes.b: columnar-final — accent stays on the stem-final syllable in all its grades; it surfaces on the ending/fused syllable only where that final loses or merges its syllabicity (fusion §316a, semivowelization §319, syncope §318c/§423, ṛ→r §372), plus the Vedic gen.pl in -nā́m (§319a). Zaliznyak-b analog (ending-tending oxytone).
schemes.c: fully mobile (hysterodynamic) — strong cases on the stem, ALL weak cases on the ending (§317, §390, §350). The monosyllabic type. Nearest Zaliznyak analog: c/f mobile classes.
schemes.d: weakest-mobile (proterokinetic edge) — strong AND middle cases on the stem(-final); ONLY the weakest cases shift to the ending (§318, §423, §446).
schemes.f: lexically irregular — accent behavior is a property of the lemma, not the class (gó §361c, nṛ́ §372, śván/yúvan §427, the §390a/b lists); see lexical_exceptions.
schemes.mapping_note: Sanskrit case-mobility is quality-driven (strong/middle/weakest), not number-driven like Russian (sg vs pl), so Zaliznyak's six letters over-specify: a/b/c/d/f above are the honest native inventory. Letters keep Zaliznyak's SPIRIT (a=fixed-stem, b=ending-tending, c/d=mobile, f=irregular) so the ZALIZNYAK_INDEX token stays one char.

rules.name: Vocative — first syllable, only when initial
rules.condition: Accented ONLY at the beginning of a sentence / metrical division (pāda); elsewhere accentless-enclitic (§314c). A qualifier phrase forms one accentual unit with its vocative (§314d); coordinate vocatives at pāda-start are each accented (§314e). Vedic split-semivowel vocatives take the accent on the first vowel element, surfacing as circumflex on the written syllable (dyāùs, §314b).
rules.encoded_behavior: voc = first_syllable if pāda/sentence-initial, else no accent. 'As a rule without exception' (§314a).

interpretation.issue: Is the vocative part of the paradigm's mobility scheme?
interpretation.decision: No — encoded as an independent positional slot; the scheme letters ignore it. The validator must exclude non-pāda-initial vocatives entirely (they are unaccented by syntax, not by paradigm).
interpretation.rationale: §314c makes accentedness a function of sentence position (enclisis), which no per-lemma scheme can carry; §314f shows Whitney himself brackets the vocative out of his paradigm accent statements.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Folding vocative into the strong-case row — rejected because it would score every mid-pāda unaccented vocative as a rule failure.

rules.name: Barytone polysyllables — accent fixed throughout
rules.encoded_behavior: If the stem is accented on the penult or further back, the accent remains on that syllable through the whole inflection (vocative aside). This is the default that removes ~all barytone lemmas from the mobility question.
exceptions: A few numeral stems deviate: §315a → §483 (out of nominal-lexicon scope; numerals excluded from the axis).

rules.name: Strong-case endings never attract the accent; fusion is phonology, not mobility
rules.encoded_behavior: N/A.sg, N/A.du, N.pl endings are accented ONLY when stem-final vowel + ending vowel merge into one syllable: plain blend keeps the acute (dattá+as → dattā́s, dattá+āu → dattāú), semivowelization yields independent svarita (nadī́+as → nadyàs, nadī́+āu → nadyāù).

interpretation.decision: Encoded as their own value 'fused' with tone derived from mechanism (acute on blend, svarita on semivowelization), kept distinct from true mobility.
interpretation.rationale: §316a derives these purely from sandhi of stem+ending; calling them mobility would make immobile b-stems look mobile in exactly the strong cases Whitney says never shift. The validator scores the surface syllable position, which 'fused' predicts exactly.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: accent='ending' for fused strong cases — rejected: it misstates Whitney's system and would corrupt the scheme assignment (b-stems misread as c).

rules.name: Weak-ending accentability gradient (framing rule)
rules.encoded_behavior: Vowel-initial (weakest) endings take the accent more readily than consonant-initial (middle) endings: nāvā́ AND nāubhís (monosyllable: both shift) vs mahatā́ BUT mahádbhis (polysyllable: only weakest shifts). Not an operative rule itself — it licenses the c vs d split that R05/R10 operationalize.

rules.name: Monosyllabic stems — ending accented in ALL weak cases

overrides.A.pl: variant — default stem, lexical minority ending (D1)

rules.encoded_behavior: The accent falls upon the ending in all the weak cases, middle and weakest alike: nāvā́, nāubhyā́m, nāvā́m, nāuṣú; vācí, vāgbhís, vācā́m, vākṣú.

interpretation.issue: D1 — the accusative plural. §317 makes A.pl a weak case (→ ending), but §317a: 'in the acc. pl. the stem is even oftener accented than the ending, some words also admitting either accentuation'; §390a gives the ending-accenting minority ('hardly more than a third'); §361a says nāú A.pl is like the nominative.
interpretation.decision: Default A.pl = stem (nom-like); the §390a lemma list overrides to ending (datás, pathás, padás, nidás, apás, uṣás, jñāsás, puṁsás, māsás, mahás) or to free variation (vācás/vā́cas, srucás, hrutás, sridhás, kṣapás, vipás, durás, iṣás, dviṣás, druhás). Both lists carried in lexical_exceptions.
interpretation.rationale: Whitney's own quantified qualification beats his own headline rule: a majority-stem default mispredicts a minority; an ending default would mispredict ~2/3 of stems. The variation lemmas must score EITHER position as correct.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Uniform A.pl = ending per bare §317 — rejected as directly contradicted by §317a/§390a/§361a.

exceptions: Retainers that keep stem accent through the weak cases: gó (§361c), dyó (§361d), nṛ́/stṛ́ (§372), śván/yúvan (§427), monosyllabic ā-root-stems (§350) — see lexical_exceptions and R07.
Sporadic stem-accented weak forms + ending-accented strong forms: §390b list.

rules.name: Monosyllabic ī/ū-stems — monosyllabic accent, A.pl like nominative

overrides.optional_fuller_endings: ending (dhiyāí, dhiyā́s, dhiyā́m loc.; later language only — §349: never in the Veda except bhiyāí RV once)

rules.encoded_behavior: ī→iy, ū→uv before vowel endings with the ending accented (dhiyā́, bhuvā́); middle cases ending-accented (dhībhís, bhūbhyás, dhīṣú); A.pl = nominative (dhíyas); G.pl freely dhiyā́m or dhīnā́m.
examples: dhī́s, dhíyam, dhiyā́, dhiyé, dhiyás, dhiyí; dhībhyā́m, dhiyós; dhíyas, dhībhís, dhiyā́m/dhīnā́m, dhīṣú (§351)

interpretation.issue: D11 — §351's paradigm accents A.sg dhíyam/bhúvam on the STEM while I.sg dhiyā́ shifts; and the du./pl. N.A. dhíyāu/dhíyas are stem-accented. Is A.sg weak here?
interpretation.decision: A.sg/A.du/N.pl/A.pl encoded stem-accented exactly as printed (strong cases + the A.pl=nom rule); only I/D/Ab-G/L sg, G-L du, G.pl and the middle cases shift.
interpretation.rationale: The §351 paradigm is explicit per form; §350's 'all the weak cases except the accus. pl.' confirms. A.sg is a strong case (§311a) so it never shifted to begin with.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Treating every non-N.sg form of a monosyllable as ending-accented — rejected against the printed paradigm.

exceptions: Fuller singular endings āi/ās/ām are post-Vedic (§349) — the RV validator must not expect them.

rules.name: Monosyllabic ā-root-stems — accent fixed on the stem
rules.encoded_behavior: Against the general monosyllabic rule, ā-stems keep the accent on the stem throughout: jā́, jā́m, jā́ (I.sg), jé, jás, jí; jā́bhis, jā́su, jā́nām.
examples: jā́ f. progeny: jā́bhis, jā́su, jā́nām (§351)

interpretation.issue: §350 hedges: 'the ā-stems APPEAR (the instances are extremely few) to keep the accent upon the stem throughout'; §351a admits the jā́ paradigm is 'rather arbitrarily extended' from four attested cases.
interpretation.decision: Encode fixed-stem (scheme a) but confidence=low; flag the whole cell as thin-evidence so a validation miss here downgrades the cell, not the ruleset.
interpretation.rationale: It is Whitney's stated best reading of the evidence; the alternative has zero textual support.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Assimilating ā-monosyllables to the c-scheme of dhī́/bhū́ — rejected: contradicts §350's explicit exception, though only weakly attested.

rules.name: Root-final ī/ū as last member of a compound — accent never thrown forward
rules.encoded_behavior: Compounds in -dhī́, -bhū́ etc. retain the accent throughout; when ī/ū is written as y/v the resulting syllable is svarita (-dhyàm, -bhvā̀); the dissyllabic writing (-dhíyam, -bhúvam) keeps the acute on the stem vowel. G.pl -dhíyām/-dhī́nām stays on the stem either way.

interpretation.issue: In the Veda the y/v spellings are 'only graphic' — always read dissyllabically (§352b).
interpretation.decision: Predict acute-on-stem-vowel for the Vedic validator (dissyllabic reading), svarita spelling accepted as an orthographic equivalent of the same position.
interpretation.rationale: §352b says the two forms differ only graphically in the Veda; position, the primary comparandum, is identical.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Scoring svarita-written forms as a different accent position — rejected: penalizes orthography, not grammar.

rules.name: Polysyllabic oxytone consonant stems — DEFAULT is columnar (no shift)
rules.encoded_behavior: 'Of polysyllabic stems ending in consonants, only a few shift the accent' — so the default is NO mobility: marút keeps ú in every case (marútā, marúte, marútas, marútām, marútsu). Only the R10 groups shift.
examples: marút: marútam, marútā, marúdbhis, marútām, marútsu (§391)

interpretation.issue: D6 — §318's headline could be read as 'polysyllabic consonant stems shift in the weakest cases', with the list as examples.
interpretation.decision: The §318a–c enumeration is EXHAUSTIVE-by-intent ('Such are:'), everything else columnar; sporadics (§318d) are lexical, not systematic.
interpretation.rationale: §318 head says 'only a few'; the §391 marút paradigm — Whitney's own chosen model of polysyllabic inflection — is fully columnar.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Weakest-shift for ALL oxytone consonant stems — rejected: contradicts 'only a few' and the marút model; would wrongly predict *marutā́.

exceptions: §318d: 'other sporadic cases will be noticed under the different declensions' — captured per-class (R15 ṛ-stems, R17 an-stems, R18 nt-stems) and per-lemma (lexical_exceptions).
§318e: adverbially used case-forms may change accent (§1110 ff.) — out of scope.

rules.name: The shifting few — weakest-only shift for -ánt participles, mahánt-type, syncopating stems
rules.encoded_behavior: Present participles in -ánt/-át (tudatā́, tudatós, tudatā́m BUT tudádbhyām, tudátsu); participle-shaped adjectives (mahatā́, bṛhatás); stems whose accented final syllable syncopates (majjñā́, mūrdhné, dāmnás → §423).

rules.name: Polysyllabic oxytone short-vowel stems (a/i/u) — retain while the final keeps its syllable

overrides.weakest_condition: stem_final if the final vowel keeps syllabic identity (datténa, agnínā, agnáye, dattébhyas, agníbhis); ending/fused if blended (dattāís, dhenāú, agnī́n, dhenū́s) or semivowelized (dhenvā́, jāmyós, bāhvós)

rules.encoded_behavior: Columnar on the final vowel; the only 'movement' is phonological loss of that syllable into the ending.

rules.name: Genitive plural -nā́m — the ending takes the accent for oxytone í/ú/ṛ́ stems (Vedic: always)
rules.encoded_behavior: ām of G.pl 'may, and in the older language always does, take the accent, though separated by n from the stem'. Stems in á do NOT follow (devā́nām keeps the lengthened stem-final) — only numerals do (§483a: saptānā́m, daśānā́m; numerals out of axis scope).

interpretation.issue: D2 — 'may, and in the older language always does': optional later, obligatory in the Veda.
interpretation.decision: Encode G.pl = ending as the categorical Vedic value (the axis and the validator are Vedic-only); annotate 'later language optional' for any future Classical use.
interpretation.rationale: The validation corpus is the RV; §319a is unambiguous for that register.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: stem_final default with ending as variant — rejected for the Vedic axis; it is the CLASSICAL citation-form convention, not the RV fact.

rules.name: Derivative long-vowel stems (ā/ī/ū) — like short-vowel stems, except G.pl … (the recorded contradiction)

accent.weakest: stem_final (svarita where semivowelized: nadyàm read nadíam)

overrides.G.pl (T2 ā-stems): stem_final (senā́nām) — §320's 'not thrown forward' holds unchallenged for ā-stems
overrides.G.pl (T4/T6 ī/ū-stems): variant — primary ending (-īnā́m: bahvīnā́m, §319a 'in RV … usually'); secondary stem_final (-ī́nām: nadī́nām, tanū́nām as printed in §356)

rules.encoded_behavior: Treatment identical to §319 stems 'save that the tone is not thrown forward upon the ending in gen. plural' (§320) — but Whitney's own §319a and his own §356 paradigm disagree for ī/ū-stems; encoded as a variant cell.
examples: nadī́, tanū́ (T4/T6): nadī́nām, tanū́nām (§356) — vs the §319a shift

interpretation.issue: D3 — the one place the cited sections SELF-CONTRADICT. §320: derivative long-vowel stems do not throw the G.pl accent forward. §319a: 'In RV., even derivative ī-stems show usually the same shift: bahvīnā́m.' §356's own Vedic paradigm prints nadī́nām/tanū́nām (no shift).
interpretation.decision: Variant cell, per-lemma. Primary prediction = ending (-īnā́m) for derivative FEMININE ADJECTIVE ī-stems (bahvī́-type, §355b's accent-shifted feminines); stem_final (-ī́nām) accepted as correct for noun-type lemmas (nadī́, tanū́). The validator scores the cell per-lemma and reports the empirical split — this cell is a measurement target, not a settled rule.
interpretation.rationale: §319a's 'usually' is a frequency claim about RV that Whitney demonstrably did not reconcile with §320 (a later-language-oriented summary) or with his §356 lemma choice. Both positions are Whitney-licensed; forcing one value would mis-score the other sub-class by design.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: (i) Categorical ending per §319a — rejected: contradicted by Whitney's own printed nadī́nām. (ii) Categorical stem per §320 — rejected: contradicted by his explicit RV usage note. A recorded variant with a validation hook is the only faithful encoding.

rules.name: Vedic polysyllabic root-declension ī/ū-stems — columnar with dissyllabic readings

stem_classes: T4/T6 (Vedic root-declension polysyllables: nadī́-type as inflected in RV)

accent.weakest: stem_final (read dissyllabically: nadíam, tanúā; written nadyàm etc. with svarita)

overrides.G.pl: stem_final as printed (rathī́nām, nadī́nām, tanū́nām) — subject to the R13/D3 variant

rules.encoded_behavior: The RV inflection of these ~70 ī- and ~dozen ū-stems keeps the acute on the stem-final vowel in its dissyllabic reading throughout; no case-driven mobility.
examples: nadī́s, nadíam, nadíā, nadíe, nadías; nadī́bhis, nadī́nām, nadī́ṣu (§356)

interpretation.issue: The written text semivowelizes (nadyàm) where the meter demands two syllables; which is the comparandum?
interpretation.decision: Predict the accent on the stem vowel under the dissyllabic reading; treat a svarita on the written contracted syllable as the SAME position (as in R08/D5).
interpretation.rationale: §356b: the contracted spellings 'are written above according to their true phonetic form' — Whitney's own paradigm is given in the dissyllabic reading.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Scoring written svarita syllables as ending-accented — rejected: orthographic artifact.

rules.name: ṛ-stems — columnar on the final in all grades; ending when ṛ loses syllabicity; G.pl shifts

accent.weakest: ending where ṛ → r (pitrā́, pitré, pitrós; dātrā́, dātré); Ab-G.sg -úr carries it on the ur syllable (pitúr, dātúr); L.sg on the ári syllable (pitári, dātári)

rules.encoded_behavior: 'If on the final of the stem, [the accent] continues, as acute, on the corresponding syllable throughout' — read as: the stem-final SYLLABLE in whatever grade — 'except in the gen. pl.' and 'where, in the weakest cases, ṛ becomes r, the ending has the accent.'
examples: pitṛ́: pitā́, pitáram, pitrā́, pitúr, pitári, pitṛ́bhis, pitṝṇā́m, pitṛ́ṣu (§373)
dātṛ́: dātā́, dātā́ram, dātrā́, dātúr, dātári, dātṛ́bhis, dātṝṇā́m (§373)
barytone contrast: svásā, svásāram, svásrā, svásur, svásṝṇām (scheme a, R02)

interpretation.issue: D8 — what is the 'corresponding syllable' when the stem-final surfaces as ar/ār/ur/ári?
interpretation.decision: The stem-final syllable under ablaut: pitá-ram, dātā́-ram, pitú-r, pitá-ri all count as stem_final; only true desyllabification (ṛ→r before vowel) hands the accent to the ending.
interpretation.rationale: The §373 paradigms accent exactly the graded final syllable in every strong/middle form; treating 'corresponding syllable' as a fixed segment would leave those forms unpredicted.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Reading Ab-G.sg pitúr / L.sg pitári as ending-accented — rejected as a false mobility signal: -ur/-ari CONTAIN the stem-final r; Whitney presents them as the acute 'continuing'. Validator note: for these two slots position-scoring is insensitive to the choice; the encoding matters only for scheme assignment.

exceptions: nṛ́ and stṛ́ 'do not show the monosyllabic accent': nṛ́bhis, nṛ́ṣu — middle cases stay on the stem; but G.pl nṛṇā́m (Veda; also narā́m §371h,i). stṛ́ defective (§371k).
usṛ́: gen. usrás, acc.pl usrás, loc. usrā́m — analogic to ī/ū-stems (§371j).

rules.name: Consonant monosyllables — the §317 rule restated, with the A.pl carve-out

overrides.A.pl: variant — default stem; §390a minority list = ending; §390a second list = free variation (D1)

rules.encoded_behavior: vā́c-model: vā́k, vā́cam, vācā́, vācé, vācás, vācí; vāgbhyā́m, vācós; vā́cas, vācás/vā́cas (A.pl), vāgbhís, vācā́m, vākṣú. pád adds stem gradation (pā́dam vs padā́) without changing the accent rule.

interpretation.issue: Same D1 as R05 (A.pl); plus §390b's two-way leak list.
interpretation.decision: As R05/D1. The §390b sporadics (weak-case stem accents sádā, tánā, ráṇe, kṣámi, sū́rā …; strong-case ending accents mahás N.pl, kāsám; preṣā́ mis-parsed as simple stem) are carried as lexical_exceptions, never generalized.
interpretation.rationale: Whitney marks them 'exceptional instances' — per-lemma noise, exactly what the exception registry is for.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: Deriving sub-rules from §390b (e.g. 'infinitive datives retain') — rejected: over-fitting a list Whitney himself presents as unsystematic.

exceptions: añc-stem accent anomalies flagged to §410 (out of cited scope; see matrix T8c).

rules.name: an/man/van-stems — the accent follows the surviving suffix syllable

accent_position: oxytone (accented suffix á: ātmán, mūrdhán, majján)
applies_to.note: barytones (rā́jan, nā́man, bráhman) are plain R02/scheme a: rā́jñā, rā́jñām keep the root accent

overrides.weakest_condition: if the suffix á is syncopated → ending (mūrdhnā́, mūrdhné, mūrdhnás, mūrdhnā́m, majjñā́, dāmnás); if the a is retained (obligatory after consonant clusters §421b, usual in the Veda §425b/f, optional in loc.sg §421b) → the suffix syllable keeps it (ātmánā, ātmáni, mūrdháni, bhū́manā-type only when barytone)

rules.encoded_behavior: Mobility is not a property of the case but of the syncope: 'when, in the weakest cases, an acute á of the suffix is lost, the tone is thrown forward upon the ending' (§423).
examples: ātmán: ātmā́, ātmā́nam, ātmánā (a retained), ātmáni; ātmábhis, ātmánām (§424)
mūrdhán: mūrdhnā́, mūrdhné, mūrdhnás, mūrdhnā́m; loc. mūrdhní OR mūrdháni (§424a)

interpretation.issue: D7 — the same case slot (e.g. I.sg) is stem-accented in ātmánā but ending-accented in mūrdhnā́; and the Veda usually keeps the a (§425b/f) where the later language drops it.
interpretation.decision: Encode the weakest slot as CONDITIONAL on syncope, with both surface shapes predicted; the validator matches whichever shape the attested form shows and scores the accent for THAT shape. G.pl ātmánām (a retained, §424) vs mūrdhnā́m (syncopated) both follow automatically.
interpretation.rationale: §423 states the condition explicitly; a per-case constant cannot be faithful. §425f: retained-a weakest forms (bhū́manā, dā́mane, ukṣáṇas) are common in the Veda — a syncope-blind rule would fail exactly there.
interpretation.rejected_alternative: weakest=ending across T8n oxytones — rejected: wrong for every retained-a form (ātmánā, mūrdháni), i.e. for the STATISTICALLY DOMINANT Vedic shapes.

exceptions: śván/yúvan: weakest stems contract to śún/yū́n WITH RETAINED accent: śúnā, śúne, yū́nā (§427) — lexical.
§426 non-lengthening lemmas (pūṣán, aryamán, ukṣán, yóṣan, vṛ́ṣan, tmán): stem shape differs, accent rule unaffected (pūṣṇā́ follows syncope rule).
§425e abbreviated instrumentals (mahinā́, variṇā́ …): accent on ending, consistent with syncope.

Unlike the §409a prā́ñc-type group (ápāñc, ávāñc, párāñc, arvā́ñc, adharā́ñc — stem accent RETAINED even when the stem contracts to ī/ū, e.g. arvā́cī, satrā́cīm, kadrī́cī all scored 100% in the H063/H115 sample), this group SHIFTS the accent onto the ending whenever the surface form is built from the contracted ī/ū allomorph. §410 states the shift explicitly and names pratīcā́, anūcás, samīcī́ as attested RV examples. Critically, per §407b ('the feminine is made by adding ī to the stem-form used in the weakest cases, and is accented like them'), this contracted allomorph is not confined to the T8c per_case 'weakest' slot — ALL feminine-gender forms of this subgroup, in ANY case/number (NOM/ACC.du samīcī́, NOM.pl samīcī́ḥ, NOM.sg śvitīcī́), take the weakest-slot accent (ending), not the strong/middle-slot stem_final value the generic T8c rule predicts. H115 (05-07-2026) confirmed this against the H063 VedaWeb sample: all 17 T8c·oxytone rule_error forms (14 samyaYc, 2 anvaYc, 1 SvityaYc) are exactly these feminine/contracted forms, and recomputing them under the weakest-slot prediction resolves the cell from 82.0% (77/94) to 100% (94/94); every masculine/neuter form and every non-shifting §409a-type lemma (arvAYc, aDarAYc, satrAYc, daDyaYc, devadryaYc, kadryaYc) was already correctly predicted.
